indicators.note: the bone is found inside the burial mound, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a tumulus is an ancient burial mound
a rib is a bone of the chest

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a decaying bone inside an ancient burial mound.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a bone in a burial mound is exactly what you would expect; 'Crumbling' is the definition, not a description of the bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moribund is in terminal decline, close to collapse, as a crumbling empire or building is.

clue.text: Disregard sweetheart, upset with small boobs

parts.note: to miss something is to overlook or disregard it

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: pet is a term of endearment, a sweetheart
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone ignores a lover who is upset about her small breasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boobs' looks like slang for breasts but is the verb or noun for blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: Boobs are blunders or mistakes, which is what missteps are.

clue.text: Counter in bank accepting payment's principal

indicators.note: accepting means the word for bank takes the letter inside it

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them

indicators.note: principal, meaning chief or first, picks out the initial letter

explanation.surface: A cashier at a bank counter accepts the main part of a payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a bank counter; it is a response that counters something.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply answers back, so it counters or responds to what was said.

parts.note: suggests covering up for the priests' misdeeds, but means a literal head covering they wear

explanation.walkthrough: Covering for someone sounds like protecting them; here it is headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap with ridges worn by Roman Catholic priests.

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is lifted upwards, reading from the bottom

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: A school's prestige has risen.
explanation.definitionFit: Note can mean distinction or eminence, as in a person of note.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to pass round the edge of something
second meaning: garments hanging from the waist

explanation.surface: Someone wanders about dressed in women's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single sentence about cross-dressing; it splits into a verb sense and a noun sense of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt is to avoid by going round the edge; skirts are also the familiar female garment.

indicators.note: includes says the answer sits inside the words just before it

parts.note: the letters run from inside the city name into the next word

explanation.surface: Turkey's capital Ankara mainly takes in a city that used to be a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, a tempting false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Karachi was Pakistan's first capital before the government moved to Islamabad.

clue.text: Rock group make time for artist

parts.note: REM is an American rock band
a make is a brand of product

explanation.surface: A rock band decides to make time for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was the great seventeenth-century Dutch painter.

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the host word underneath the abbreviation

parts.note: SM is the abbreviation for sadomasochism
a host is a great number, an army

explanation.surface: An obsequious host backs a taste for sadomasochism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' looks like a party host; it is the old sense of an army.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy describes oily, ingratiating flattery, just like fawning behaviour.

clue.text: Backing dogs concerning Manx cat legend

indicators.note: backing means the whole string of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: rats, like dogs, are contemptible people or scoundrels
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is an informal word for a cat

explanation.surface: Someone backs racing dogs and a famous Manx cat, as if placing bets.
explanation.walkthrough: PUSS without its tail is PUS; RATS + RE + PUS is then read backwards. 'Backing' looks like gambling support, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend in this sense is a celebrated person, a star of exceptional fame.

indicators.note: periodically takes every other letter of the word orderly

parts.note: to earn is to get money in payment for work

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly now and then gets promoted to master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a hospital worker, but only its second, fourth and sixth letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To relearn something is to master or acquire a skill a second time.

indicators.note: before places the drink in front of the next piece

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: de-tailed, with its tail or last letter removed

parts.note: a bar is a pole or rod

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink before a detailed pole-dancing routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'elaborate' but means losing the tail, so BAR becomes BA.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance in quick rhythm.

parts.note: to seek to do something is to try
Valentine is an example of a saint, ST, so Valentine's is ST'S; perhaps marks the example

explanation.surface: A lover seeks romantic dates on Valentine's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: Valentine is a saint, so 'Valentine's' gives the abbreviation ST plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: Trysts are romantic secret meetings between lovers, so they are a kind of date.

clue.text: Pick fruit eating each tart, oddly

indicators.note: eating means the fruit swallows the next letters, which go inside it

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone picks out fruit to eat along with a tart, which is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' looks like a verb about choosing fruit; it is the noun for a guitar pick.
explanation.definitionFit: A plectrum is the small flat piece used to pluck guitar strings, commonly called a pick.

clue.text: Raising hat, single chap is earnest

indicators.note: raising in a down clue lifts the word up, so it is read backwards

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gent is a chap or gentleman

explanation.surface: A single man raises his hat in an earnest greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligent means hardworking and conscientious, showing earnest effort.

clue.text: Sell-off with one put into poverty

indicators.note: into means the two pieces are placed inside the word for poverty

parts.note: privation is lack of necessities, poverty
I is the Roman numeral for one
sat, as in sat the baby on the chair, means put or placed

explanation.surface: A sell-off leaves someone plunged into poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' does double duty in the surface but gives SAT (placed) here, with 'into' signalling the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Privatisation is the selling off of state-owned industry to private buyers.

clue.text: Audacious pinching head of Venus bust

indicators.note: pinching means the word for audacious grabs and holds the letter inside it

parts.note: insolent means cheekily audacious

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the goddess's name

explanation.surface: Someone cheekily steals the head of a bust of Venus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a sculpture of Venus but is the adjective meaning broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or firm that has gone bust cannot pay its debts, which is what insolvent means.

clue.text: After credit money's not all there

indicators.note: after puts the money word following the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
ackers is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Once the credit is gone, someone's money doesn't add up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ackers is old British slang for cash, said to come from Egyptian piastres.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is informal for crazy, describing someone mentally unbalanced.

parts.note: suggests Wellington at the battle, but Waterloo here is the London railway terminus and its man in charge

explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo suggests the 1815 battle and Wellington; it is London's Waterloo railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: The official in charge of a railway station holds this title, which fits a London terminus named after the battle.

indicators.note: housing means the word for like contains the next word

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
to untie is to free or loosen

explanation.surface: Relatives who like free accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunties are relatives, the sisters of one's parents.

parts.note: at means present at or taking part in, as at a party
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: Someone involved in a robbery has doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 2,5 the answer reads as being at a heist, which fits the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist rejects belief in God, a person who doubts divine existence.

clue.text: Movies with spies tackling flipping army

indicators.note: tackling means the spies grab hold of the next piece, which sits inside

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency

indicators.note: flipping means the word for army is turned round

parts.note: men are soldiers, an army

explanation.surface: Spies in a film take on a flipping great army.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema means films collectively, the movies as an art or industry.

parts.note: the first Man is the Isle of Man, so its man is a native of an island

explanation.walkthrough: A 'man's man' is a macho type, but the capital M hides the Isle of Man, whose inhabitants live on an island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant of any island, including the Isle of Man, is described by this word.

indicators.note: captures means the image word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: pic is a short form of picture, an image
burning means very hot

explanation.surface: A photograph captures something burning in a blaze of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Photic is a technical adjective meaning relating to light, as in the photic zone of the ocean.

indicators.note: capsized in a down clue means the whole sequence is turned upside down

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
the Dart is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: A boat in an eastern river has overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat in the surface; it means a skilled occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a skilled job or occupation, such as a craft.

clue.text: Cheese being runny is enjoyable, primarily

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A cheese being runny is above all what makes it enjoyable.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cow's-milk cheese that is prized when ripe and runny.

clue.text: Extract largely employed making ink initially

definitions.text: Extract largely employed making ink initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the five words in the clue

explanation.surface: A substance is extracted and mostly used for making ink.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the resin is an extract used in making some inks.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin extracted from tropical trees and used in varnishes, inks and ointments.

indicators.note: consuming means the insect eats, holding the next letters inside it

parts.note: a termite is an insect

indicators.note: insides picks the two central letters of banana

explanation.surface: An order to stop an insect eating the inside of a banana.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to bring it to an end, to halt it.

clue.text: Confirm a teetotaller holds name back

indicators.note: holds means the teetotaller abbreviation contains the following piece

parts.note: TT is the abbreviation for teetotal or a teetotaller

indicators.note: back means the word for name is read in reverse

parts.note: to set, as in set a date, is to name or fix

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that a teetotaller is keeping a name back.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness that something is true, to vouch for it.

clue.text: Section of trestle's stood on edge

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a trestle table stood on its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless means unable to settle, nervous and agitated.
